notes.title: Free Update 1.3: Roles & Schemes is now live!
notes.content:
Hi everyone!

Ready to expand your criminal empire with a whole new host of abilities and activities? Then good news - our latest [b]FREE 1.3 Update[/b] “[i]Roles & Schemes[/i]” - is now available!

As your Captains work to grow your empire, they’ll pick up their own, unique experiences. You can now use that experience to elevate them to a new Role in your crew. Once they’re in a role, they’ll be able to start their own Schemes - ongoing activities that will give you an opportunity to make some big scores. You’ll use the new organization chart to see each crew member and Captain and their progress toward a Role. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38625768/a96590ba104f699d9a9b391f849a7298b0447a0a.png[/img]

Each Role also comes with unique abilities. For example, Intimidators can help you discover what rival gangs are storing in their hideouts, while Accountants will help you purchase buildings at cheaper rates. All Captains are eligible for promotion into a Role and you can have several of the same Role.

Based on their experience and Role, your promoted Captains will have some ideas of their own that they’ll want to pitch to you as the Boss. Once you agree to one of their cunning Schemes - and after some investment on your part - they’ll get down to business.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38625768/2ceceb4d969bcc0804599600857c91f56319d7fc.png[/img]

Schemes come with risks as well as a variety of rewards, each depending on what you choose to have your Captain do, so choose carefully. Get it right and the rewards will be worth the risk. Get it wrong and all your investment will go down the drain, or worse - your Captain could get arrested or killed.

We’d love to know how you’re enjoying the latest update, so as always you can find us over on [url=https://twitter.com/CityOfGangsters]Twitter[/url] and [url=https://discord.gg/cityofgangsters]Discord[/url].

Hope to see you there!

Matt & Rob
SomaSim

notes.title: Announcing free update 1.3 “Roles & Schemes” + new Criminal Record DLC!
notes.content:
Hey everyone, since our last post we’ve been hard at work on some new mechanics and content for City of Gangsters, and today we’re announcing the impending arrival of [b]Roles and Schemes[/b] in the main game! 

These new systems will be released in [b]free update[/b] 1.3, arriving in [u][b]early March[/b][/u]. You will be able to [b]specialize your captains[/b] into specific [b]roles[/b], gain access to a variety of new abilities and actions, which we’re calling [b]schemes[/b], and inspect your entire outfit in a new [b]organization chart[/b].

Along with version 1.3, we will be launching a new DLC which extends these new mechanics! Unfolding in the streets of Philadelphia, [i][b]City of Gangsters: Criminal Record[/b][/i] will not only [b]add more[/b] roles and schemes, but also provide a [b]new city map[/b], with a fascinating novel starting condition, and a brand new view of [b]“Your Office”[/b] where you will collect mementos of your various criminal deeds and exploits.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38625768/5f1f74b34187eddbb85750d5492c5b6ca7175268.png[/img]
[b]The times have changed [/b]

[b]Captain roles[/b] let you specialize your crew further. Your new and improved outfits will be more diverse and adaptable with their own distinct hierarchy and feel. Once a crew member gains enough experience and ascends to [b]captain[/b] level, they’ll have the opportunity to work towards an advanced role such as:

[list]
[*] Enforcer
[*] Intimidator 
[*] Jailbird
[*] Lookout
[*] Mouthpiece 
[*] Closer
[*] Accountant  
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38625768/a96590ba104f699d9a9b391f849a7298b0447a0a.png[/img]

Attaining a specialized role requires very specific experience and expertise, which differs from role to role. For example, to become an [b]enforcer[/b], a candidate must have been successful at a number of combat and enforcement operations in the past, in addition to attaining the rank of a captain. And remember, a captain can only have one role, so choose wisely!

[b]The less I say the more my work gets done[/b]

These roles in turn unlock [b]role-specific abilities[/b]. As your gang moves through the 1920s, you will discover that your new captains will develop ideas for their own personal [b]schemes[/b]. Maybe they will want to stage a bank robbery or blackmail a local crooked cop, based on their prior experience. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38625768/2ceceb4d969bcc0804599600857c91f56319d7fc.png[/img]

Schemes are elaborate illicit activities that [b]unfold over a number of stages[/b], and each stage has a number of different options and potential consequences. Will you be able to leverage the scheme to your long-term advantage? Or will your captain fall prey to their own ambitions, the law, or your rivals?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38625768/02bf977d1187765ec0907a0b29d8b2aa82c259ec.png[/img]

[b]Philadelphia freedom[/b]

Beyond update 1.3, the Criminal Record DLC will bring extra roles and schemes into the game, along with some new content. It also unlocks the [b]city of Philadelphia[/b], with a unique starting condition that is sure to be incredibly profitable. And no matter which city you pick, you will now be able to [b]set up an office[/b], in a country lodge or in a downtown penthouse, and it will fill up over time with spoils of victory and mementos of your escapades.

[b]Shine the light[/b]

We can’t wait for you to dig into these new mechanics, and develop your crew into a highly specialized criminal machine! We’ll be back soon with another update to break down the new systems and discuss the additions in City of Gangsters: Criminal Record, so take care of yourselves until then! 

Matt & Rob
SomaSim

notes.title: Prohibition Encyclopedia Update & future plans
notes.content:
Hi everyone, we wanted to give one last update for the year, and talk a bit about what’s coming up in 2022!

[u][b]Prohibition encyclopedia update[/b][/u]
 
The in-game Prohibition encyclopedia is a great tool for learning all about the systems, resources, operations and skills that you’ll discover while running your outfit. We’ve now expanded it further to include:

[b]Weapons -[/b] A full list of the weapons that you can acquire including stats and costs.

[b]Region specific resources & operations -[/b] You can now learn more about bootlegging opportunities specific to each of the city maps.   

[b]Crew skills -[/b] An updated list of all the crew skills that can be learned in the game, including those that relate to gambling houses and their associated activities.  

[b]Gambling houses -[/b] A breakdown of the possible gambling house operations that you can set up, including Atlantic City’s casinos.

[b]Operation expansions and gambling features -[/b] An overview of possible expansions and gambling house features, so you can plan in advance how to improve your operations. 

[u][b]Looking ahead[/b][/u]

Since the [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1386780/view/3104663815688797260]Gambling & Debt update[/url] released last month, we’ve been working on the next major feature, and it’s progressing very nicely. Not to spoil too much, but we’ve been noticing that a lot of you, our players, have been asking about better crew organization: how it would be interesting for your crew to progress beyond captain status, and gain access to some new criminal schemes as you take over the city.

Well, if you were asking about some of those things, we’ll have some good news for you in the new year! But - that’s all we can say right at this very moment. Stay tuned for this and a couple of other surprises in the next major update, planned for early 2022! :)

Also - if you haven’t joined us on [url=https://discord.com/invite/CityofGangsters]Discord[/url], everyone is invited! If you’ve got questions about gameplay, found a bug, have a suggestion for a future update, want to talk strategy or just hang out with some fellow players, we’ve got a great, active community over there.

So with that, we’d like to thank you all for your support of [i]City of Gangsters[/i] during its first year - from betas to demos to release day and beyond. Without your feedback from your many (and for some very many) hours of play, the game would not have become what it is now and we would not have the inspiration to carry it to even greater heights in the coming year. Truly, sincerely, thank you.

Happy Holidays all, and see you in the New Year!

Matt & Rob
SomaSim

notes.title: Free Update 1.2: Gambling & Debt is now live!
notes.content:
Hi everyone! 

Get ready to go all in with our brand new illicit gambling operations, as today we released our next free update, called version 1.2: Gambling & Debt! 

[u][b]Update 1.2: Gambling & Debt[/b][/u]

In today’s base game update, we’re adding the ability to run [b]gambling operations[/b]. You’ll be able to take over new buildings, [b]install attractive games[/b] of chance or skill, and deck them out with amenities to keep your marks playing longer and spending more money. And also, [b]keep an eye on your gamblers[/b], because if their luck runs dry and they can no longer pay off their line of credit, you’ll be able to [b]visit them at home[/b], and use your forceful argumentation style to parlay their debt into new opportunities for you.

Your diversification into gambling starts with territory. After gaining control of your 10th corner, you will be notified that an opportunity to set up a [b]gambling house[/b] has opened up. You’ll need to go and start a conversation with one of your front owners, and you’ll be able to redeem a favor to gain access to gambling opportunities.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38625768/626fb8e1b1fa60c2482c456fc3438bd62cf640b2.jpg[/img]

The front owner will show you nearby residential buildings that they know about, quiet places with pliable landlords, where you will be able to start a new gambling operation. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38625768/f62ca34d948294edc83e0ef04c8b244df98a0160.png[/img]

[b]Each location varies[/b] in how many walk-in customers it attracts from the area, which determines how busy your house will get, so choose well to maximize the number of customers visiting the establishment. But you’ll also need to consider carefully the new operation’s position relative to your other illicit businesses, because gambling operations will [b]raise heat[/b] and draw the attention of cops and rivals. 

[u][b]Managing your gambling house[/b][/u]

Once you’ve paid startup costs, you’ll gain access to an empty gambling house. To avoid police attention, there can only be one in each precinct.

You’ll immediately see that operating a gambling establishment is pretty different from the alcohol-related operations that you’ve been running.   

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38625768/65d86b4923a9f14e097af106ffa9a79e2fdc26db.jpg[/img]

To get things going, you’ll need to hire a [b]manager[/b] to run the joint and drop off some cash to fund the house. This cash will be used to support your gambling features. Each type of gambling house supports a different number of slots where you can add games and improvements.   

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38625768/6a3e454850c45497bac104a6cabb3901779be6f6.png[/img]

As is the case with backroom operations, you’ll need the right crew skills and prerequisites to be able to install each feature and to upgrade the gambling house itself.

Features come in three varieties:  

[b]Low-stakes games[/b] [i](Slot machines, policy shops, bookmaking, etc.)[/i] Draw in many walk-in players from nearby houses to place occasional bets. These have small minimum/maximum bets, with infrequent payouts and longer odds (e.g. 2% chance 25:1 payout).  

[b]High stakes games[/b] [i](Blackjack tables, roulette wheels, poker tables, etc.)[/i] Attract nearby regulars to take a seat and play for a while. They have large minimum/maximum bets, with more frequent payouts and shorter odds (e.g. 10% of a 3:1 payout). [b]Regular players and the debt that they accrue will become an important source of opportunity. [/b]

[b]Improvements[/b] [i](Small bar, imported furnishings, employee uniforms, etc.)[/i] Improve the performance and profitability of other features. 

Once you’ve installed a few features you can keep track of how your gambling houses are doing in the finances menu. In some games, gamblers play against each other and you just skim off the top. But in others, they play against the house, and you will need to be prepared with enough cash on hand to pay out if they win big.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38625768/0322b23051e8d6eaacd0ebc3824893ac037eee11.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38625768/62469607c27ffe39bdedd9bae18464858b3c3a88.png[/img]

[u][b]Debt management & risk[/b][/u] 

It goes without saying that running a gambling operation is not without risks, and the fortunes of your gambling houses may change. Regulars who play at your high-stakes games might win big and you need to be ready for that - but they’re actually more likely to run out of cash, draw up a line of credit, and then proceed to gamble it away, at which point they will find themselves in debt to you.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38625768/c2b8cebf30781972f413cdccd57ff8cdd162b4c8.jpg[/img]

Once they get in over their heads - such as $500 in the red - they will not be able to draw more credit without your permission. At this point, you’ll get a notification and map pin to go pay them a visit at home. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38625768/77818e69ecd47c5e96cfbeb722165722926a9ae3.png[/img]

When you talk to a debtor you’ll have some choices. You can:   

[b]Demand immediate payment -[/b] Tell them that they have to pay you back immediately. They will attempt to scrounge up the cash they owe you in the next few weeks. But sometimes they won’t have enough, so then it’ll be up to you to decide how benevolent you’re feeling when that day comes, and how their friends and family will react to your decision.

[b]Blackmail -[/b] Ask them for payment in kind. That could mean the keys to a new vehicle, access to a building, a delivery of rare resources, an introduction to someone useful or… Well, who knows what else they might try to sell you on to wriggle out of debt? They’ll have a few weeks to secure what they promised, so you’ll need to return later to collect. [b]IMPORTANT:[/b] The options and rewards offered change, as the person gets further and further in debt. So you can leverage this to your advantage to gain ever more valuable opportunities.

[b]Extend credit -[/b] Grant them additional credit. This can be extended to $1000 and then finally to $2000 if they get into debt again. Of course, they’ll try to press their luck and win back the debt that they owe. But honestly, they’ll just be digging the hole even deeper. 

Your biggest risk with debt collection is that a debtor might panic and decide to skip town with everything they have including the money that they owe you - and the likelihood of this happening increases the further into your debt they fall! So consider how far you want to push someone and weigh the potential rewards that you might gain.

And finally, don’t forget about the cops - because they certainly won’t be forgetting about you. Like with your bootlegging and protection rackets, gambling will increase heat and when it becomes too high, the cops will raid your gambling house, confiscate the cash stored there, and smash up one of its features for good measure. So make sure that the local cop is paid off if you want to avoid this expensive inconvenience.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38625768/09c0de22010310022fcb84997dc8b6cd4189c54d.jpg[/img]

That’s all for today, but we’d love to hear what you think about update 1.2 now that it's live. As always you can find us on [url=https://twitter.com/CityOfGangsters]Twitter[/url] and [url=https://discord.com/invite/CityofGangsters]Discord[/url] so hope to see you there! 

Until next time, 

Matt & Rob
SomaSim

notes.title: City of Gangsters: Atlantic City is available now!
notes.content:
Welcome to Atlantic City! Where a whole new world of bootlegging and illegal gambling is waiting for you.

Our Atlantic City map has been designed to showcase our new gambling and debt mechanic, along with exclusive additional content and opportunities you won’t find in any other city.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38625768/c222923ff77f0cf957f47f772bddc2c70ebdde7b.jpg[/img]

This coastal vacation town was a mecca for entertainment and booze smuggling in equal measure during the Prohibition. Which is why we’ve introduced unique gambling operations and features, including ritzy casinos and high-stakes games which are bound to ensure that your wealthy clientele continues to part ways with their cash! 

We’ve given players more freedom in Atlantic City to explore the gambling and debt mechanics by removing the one gambling house per precinct limit and by making expansion into gambling available much earlier in the game. However it won’t all be plain sailing, as the map will provide some interesting geographical challenges to overcome, so make sure to expand your relationship network wisely!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38625768/068b97da3216c8bef71586de77b1ac1145d9b225.png[/img]

Through your debtors and other contacts you’ll also be able to get your hands on lucrative new alcohol resources. These rare types of booze can be acquired by establishing firm connections among the city’s various nationalities. From Canadian whiskey to Caribbean rum, business will be booming in no time!

notes.title: City of Gangsters Developer Update #15
notes.content:
Hey everyone, we’ve got some big news to share with you! 

Today, we’re announcing the introduction of [i]gambling[/i], a major new game mechanic and additional revenue stream for your burgeoning criminal empire, which will be the central theme of our next major [b]free update[/b] in version 1.2 arriving late November.  

To coincide with this we are also releasing a new DLC! Set among the bright lights and boardwalks of ‘America’s Playground’, [i][b]City of Gangsters: Atlantic City[/b][/i] provides a showcase of these new gambling mechanics, and includes a range of additional alcohol types, bootlegging operations, crew skills to learn, a legacy goal to beat, a fresh new map to explore, and more!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38625768/6f900390d830b38ab44d2a7cfc819baae0ab5d12.png[/img]

[b]Where the sand’s turning to gold[/b]

Gambling functions both as a lucrative means of gaining income, as well as a new source of opportunities and challenges. Through your fronts you’ll gain control of new establishments such as gambling dens, card parlors, and eventually even casinos. Then once under new management, you’ll be able to start up gambling operations, including slot machines, numbers games, poker tables, roulette wheels, and many more. 

Some of these games will start attracting regular players from the neighborhood, the family members and friends of your local suppliers and customers. Regulars can spend a lot of time and money gambling in your establishments, and they can be a great source of income when they’re losing, but also a huge risk to your cashflow if they hit a lucky streak. Your floor manager will run the show, but you will have to monitor the cash situation in your various casinos and adjust accordingly.

[b]Debts that no honest man can pay[/b]

As regulars spend down their own cash reserves, they might get into debt with you, and ask you to extend credit - which they might or might not be able to pay back. Outstanding debt can be a great investment, because people who can’t pay their debts can be forced into all sorts of unscrupulous forms of repayment, including giving up prized possessions or getting involved in things that they otherwise wouldn’t want to be involved in.

But watch out, because like every investment, there will be risks. Relationships matter, and as you push people around, remember that they will talk to their friends and family, who may be your key suppliers. And if you push them too far, they might panic and completely skip town, taking their debt with them. How far are you willing to go? How much credit are you willing to extend to somebody in order to get a really good hook on them and extract extraordinary repayment? 

[b]Meet me tonight in Atlantic City[/b]

Matt & Rob

notes.title: City of Gangsters Developer Update #13
notes.content:
Hi all, we’ve got some exciting news - we just released [b][i]City of Gangsters[/i][/b] update 1.1! This is the first of a number of major content updates that we have planned. The major focus for update 1.1 is the introduction of customizable city maps.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38625768/4253b5770132163f8fe0424ccb658afb2139fdda.jpg[/img]

[u][b]Custom map editor[/b][/u]  

When you start a new game, in addition to the standard city maps you now have the option to select ‘custom map’ from the drop down.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38625768/032be031d28ada49a557de1c0d148227dc927ee7.jpg[/img]

Selecting this option takes you through to the custom map editor where you have access to a host of new options.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38625768/94447128745ff55c14f52e8b7877c1f26ba79360.png[/img]

[u][b]General options[/b][/u]

First, give your city its official name and state, and pick which city map (Chicago, Pittsburgh, Detroit, or Cincinnati) to use as a template in determining resources, operation types, and missions.

[u][b]Rivals and challenges[/b][/u]

Next, change the difficulty of your map by adjusting the number of rival outfits, troublemakers, and police precincts. As a rule of thumb, the more you have of each NPC type on the map, the more challenging it will be! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38625768/f014fad4df469ddcb9ba22233f7fa3d074e27c54.jpg[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38625768/e2db2b933af93aa7c130e05de369d032f3871586.jpg[/img]

[u][b]Topography options[/b][/u]

Want more hills? A coastline? Extra rivers? You can modify the map to include different configurations of rivers, hills, and coastlines. Adding topographic complexity creates more chokepoints and new challenges when expanding your relationship network and territory.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38625768/abbf566deb3d33abda7e8bf1c50aafbb49db7c81.jpg[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38625768/2d1e913120d1cea6a1e61fcf5654b6d4cc1378a5.jpg[/img]

[u][b]Layout options[/b][/u]

Road networks can be customized in several ways, from a strong grid reminiscent of cities like Chicago, through several other types all the way to very organic layout full of unexpected clusters, more reminiscent of cities like Boston. Additionally, you can change the proportions of industrial and commercial centers, which will change how many high level businesses of both types will be available across the city.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38625768/c68bc6c82645af5e738caf84f82213670a3bc0f1.jpg[/img]

[u][b]Steam Workshop and modding[/b][/u]

In the coming weeks we’ll also be adding initial Steam Workshop support to share your custom maps with other players. We’ve had lots of requests for modding support, and map sharing is our first step in this direction. Expect more information and instructions soon.

We hope that you’ll enjoy experimenting with these new tools and sharing your novel Prohibition cities - we can’t wait to see what you’ll come up with! 

[u][b]What’s next?[/b][/u] 

More criminal activities, you say? We’ve been thinking about how to add another layer of risk - and reward - to our Prohibition cities. We can’t reveal the exact details right now, but we’ll be sharing more information on here as soon as it’s ready.

--- 

Thank you for checking out our update!

And if you’re new to the game please come join our [url=https://discord.gg/CityofGangsters]Discord[/url] community, we have great discussions going on there, and people are posting awesome tips for getting started and running a successful outfit.

Until next time, 

Matt & Rob
Co-founders - SomaSim

notes.title: Developer Update #12 - delivery improvements, and much more!
notes.content:
Hi everybody,

In the two weeks since the last update, we've gathered a lot of feedback from the community, and have been busy turning those ideas into reality. We have a lot of ideas - for additions, for improvements and, of course, for what bugs we should squash. ;)

Since the release we've been shipping improvements several times a week, each week. This has been great, because it let us get changes into players' hands and see how well we address what you all have been telling us. Some of the big themes we've addressed in the recent releases:
[list]
[*] Deliveries have gotten a lot of attention: new delivery steps, various UI improvements, separate tutorial lesson, cost retuning, and more. This system is key to efficient mid-game, so we wanted to give it extra attention.
[*] Boss character customization - much more control over your starting character appearance and starting traits
[*] Lots of UI quality of life improvements: shift-clicks that skip to the most common interactions, new hotkeys, resources can be favorited for quick overlay toggle, and much more
[*] Various gameplay improvements: ability to install very large storage depots, more interesting police behavior, pathfinding fixes, and more
[*] Lots of tuning improvements and tweaks to quests, skills, AIs, and more
[/list]

You can see the full list here: [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/1386780/allnews/]https://steamcommunity.com/app/1386780/allnews/[/url]

It's been great to be able to respond to feedback so quickly, and we have much more planned.

And specifically, we have some [i][b]bigger[/b][/i] improvements planned - and the work on the first of those is already underway!

So to accommodate that, we'll be adjusting our schedule: you'll still see frequent updates with small improvements and bug fixes, but in addition to those, every few weeks or months we'll be shipping more major updates. We'll ship those to a beta branch first, for anyone who wants to check out a work in progress, and then release to everybody once we're happy with it.

We'll be sharing more information about each of those as they get closer. But you can expect a beta branch for [b]version 1.1 in early September.[/b]

And if you're wondering what's going to be in version 1.1... Sorry, can't tell you. Not yet. But soon. :)

Happy playing!
- Matt & Rob

notes.title: Developer Update #11
notes.content:
Hi everyone, 

We wanted to start our first post-release update by thanking you for all the support and feedback that we’ve received so far. It's been a busy few days and we have been reading through all the comments and suggestions across the Steam forums, Discord, and Twitter. The feedback is greatly appreciated [u][b]so please keep it coming![/b][/u]

In response to your feedback, we thought it would be helpful if we shared our development timeline for the next couple of weeks so you can see some of what will be arriving in-game:      

[list]
[*] [b]Warehouse depot -[/b] This suggestion was put forward by the community and will allow you to build a huge storage area in the back of one of your controlled buildings. Depots will be useful for stockpiling ingredients and booze and thus freeing up valuable inventory space within production buildings. 
[*] [b]UI streamlining around resource displays and overlays [/b]- To provide additional information and feedback to the player, and help inform decision making.
[*] [b]Additional starting character options -[/b] We’ve had a lot of requests for deeper boss character customization and this will allow you to select the traits and portrait elements more intentionally, instead of (or in addition to) rolling for randomized combinations.
[*] [b]Tutorial adjustments -[/b] We have a whole delivery system already built-in, but we don’t even teach the players how to use it. We should fix that. :)
[*] [b]Ongoing tuning and small quality of life improvements.[/b]
[*] [b]Week 1 and 2 bug fixes.[/b] 
[/list]
[u][b]In the weeks and months ahead...[/b][/u]
 
Following the first few weeks of updates we’re going to be working on our broader strategy for[b] larger quality of life improvements, additional content, and features[/b] that are requested by the community and fit within the scope of the game’s design. Like we said, we have read through a lot of player feedback already and there are definitely some really interesting ideas that we’d like to explore further so watch this space!

Finally if you are enjoying the game right now, consider leaving us a [b]review[/b], it would mean a lot to us at this early stage. We’re a tiny indie studio from Chicago that’s entirely self-supported by our games, so every review counts a lot!

Matt & Rob
SomaSim

notes.title: City of Gangsters Developer Update #10
notes.content:
Hey everyone, as promised we’re back with one last pre-release update for you. In this post we’re going to be taking a look at end game goals, and how they contribute to your legacy once prohibition ends in 1933.

[u][b]Establishing your legacy [/b][/u]

Over the course of a thirteen year campaign, you will work towards completing a variety of goals across four categories:

[list]
[*] Fame
[*] Connections
[*] Economy
[*] Competitors
[/list]
Let’s explore each of these categories and the goals associated with them:

[u][b]Fame[/b][/u]

[i]People look up to the rich and powerful, and have since the dawn of time. See how your legacy stacks up based on your wealth and power.[/i]

[b]Grasping the gilded age[/b] - Your outfit has the highest net worth of all outfits in the city, after accounting for all cash, assets, and operations.

[b]Enburdened by destiny[/b] - Your territory extends as far as the eye can see. At least 30% of the city must be under your control.

[b]Coarse and cunning[/b] - Your crew will follow you in whatever you do. At least 7 of your crew members should be at captain level.

[u][b]Connections [/b][/u]

[i]The more people you know, the more doors will open to you. See how your legacy stacks up based on your connections and favors.[/i]

[b]Collector of favors[/b] - You’ve mastered the favor economy. Your outfit has at least 15 affiliates: local business owners who owed you many favors over the years.

[b]Player with railroads[/b] - Smuggling by rail. You pulled a train depot into your territory, and used it to strike at least one illegal business deal.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38625768/ded706da64d547eea3d2553fd7b4c74cc9a047d0.jpg[/img]

[b]Nation’s freight handler[/b] - Smuggling by boat. You pulled a longshoremen’s hall into your territory, and used it to strike at least one illegal business deal.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38625768/26250efccaecdb2239bf219066f7e1fda1e78446.jpg[/img]

[u][b]Economy[/b][/u]

[i]Ruthlessness in business can fund a ritzy and glamorous lifestyle later on. See how your legacy stacks up based on your business success.[/i]

[b]Producer of alcohols[/b] - Your outfit has the most profitable manufacturing. Rankings use the total value of booze produced in the previous month, across all of your operations.

[b]Distributor to the people[/b] - Your outfit has the most profitable sales and distribution, such as bootleggers and speakeasies. Rankings use the total value of booze liquidated in the previous month, across all of your properties.

[b]Supplier to the stars[/b] - You’ve become an exclusive supplier to a ritzy downtown hotel, which became one of your tied houses.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38625768/64ebd17a389a7e2d80de479dc77d4704c347f6d6.jpg[/img]

[b]Bourbon kings (DELUXE EDITION ONLY)[/b] - Your outfit has gone local in the hills of Kentucky and has sold 500 cases of bourbon.

[u][b]Competitors [/b][/u]

[i]Some say that it is better to be feared than loved. See how your legacy stacks up based on your success in dealing with the competition.[/i]

[b]Obliterated competition[/b] - Competing outfits are few and far between, and will not cause much trouble. At least 50% of the city's outfits have been wiped from the map, through whatever means necessary.

[b]Neutralized hooligans[/b] - Corner hooligans fear you. At least 50% of the city's hooligans have been eliminated or made compliant, through whatever means necessary. 

[b]Earned the dividends of peace[/b] - You never triggered a vendetta with another outfit, such as by killing one of their people. 

Ultimately your level of victory in [i]City of Gangsters[/i] is measured by the total number of goals that you meet:   

[b]Standard victory:[/b] Reach and maintain three of these goals at the end of prohibition, and your name will be well known to anybody who’s anybody. After prohibition you will be set for life as a famous business mogul or community leader.

[b]Legendary victory:[/b] Reach and maintain six of these goals, and your wealth and savvy will become the stuff of legends. You will be known forever as the ruler of the city. 

Which goals you choose to complete are entirely up to you, and we encourage you to experiment going after different combinations to see how the game changes based on different strategies. 

[u][b]Update: Achievements[/b][/u]

We’re sure many of you will be happy to hear that we’ve added 80 achievements to discover and unlock. Best of luck to completionists among you as some of those are pretty devious!

We also wanted to take a moment to thank all of you for your enthusiasm, ideas, and support throughout the development of [i]City of Gangsters[/i]. We’re really pleased with what we have been able to achieve and can’t wait for you to experience the game yourselves! Following release, we will continue to work on updating the game to ensure that it is the very best that it can be, so please keep your feedback coming in via Discord, Twitter and in the Steam forums (we read everything!). 

Bring on Monday.

Matt & Rob
Co-founders - SomaSim

notes.title: City of Gangsters Developer Update #7
notes.content:
Hi all, in only 3 weeks you’ll be able to embark on your first [i]City of Gangsters[/i] campaign! To help you get ready, we thought we’d give you an overview of logistics and how to use the[b] automated deliveries system[/b] to streamline your resource production and distribution. On top of that, we’ll also be talking about vehicle fleet management and composition.   

[u][b]Automating deliveries[/b][/u]

Deliveries are customizable, multi-step schedules which proceed automatically every time you advance to the next turn. As your outfit grows, you’ll find deliveries are essential for ensuring a steady supply of ingredients to your production operations, and then distributing your finished booze throughout the city. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38625768/686659480b23c07aae8f89bccecbdf1a95821e08.jpg[/img]

Each new delivery needs a crew member and a vehicle. When you’re picking who’s driving, it helps to check out a crew member’s [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1386780/view/3024711605410615488]traits[/url] and see how those can be beneficial -  like reducing corner heat or boosting customer relationship levels. 

Each resource takes up a variable amount of storage capacity so you’ll also need to think about which vehicle type is best for each delivery. For example, a small truck will hold a lot more than a two-door car. So if you’re moving around lots of bulky resources, the truck is the natural choice. Trucks are however more expensive to purchase and you’ll need to acquire the correct crew skills to use them.   

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38625768/fec52792fc7e1fe4fcce4308c20073ddeda06a08.jpg[/img]

[u][b]Delivery action steps[/b][/u]

Deliveries work by linking together action steps. For each step, you’ll have the following actions to choose from:

[b]Buy/sell resources[/b] - Select a resource to display any known businesses that trade in it. Then click on an individual business to add it to the step and choose the amounts to buy or sell. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38625768/bb8ebb4879a2b58459bdef46a782c85aaaf8bd2c.jpg[/img]

[b]Storage pick up/drop off/ensure cash on hand[/b] - Select a resource to display your controlled buildings. Click on a building to add it to the delivery and choose the quantities to pick up or drop off. Ensure cash on hand is a handy shortcut that allows you to pick up set quantities of cash from a building your outfit controls.  

[b]Collect from a front[/b] - Select this action to display your fronts. Then click on a front to add it to the step. On arrival, your driver will collect all available protection money or pay them if they’re not making enough each month from protection fees. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38625768/8047f70af0be724350d1b35bf580ce6353a03e68.jpg[/img]

[u][b]Managing your vehicle fleet[/b][/u]

As you continue to use your vehicles, they’ll wear out. If a vehicle’s condition drops to zero, you won’t be able to load or unload it, so it’s important to keep on top of vehicle maintenance. The city has quite a few mechanics who will repair your cars, trucks or vans for a healthy fee.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38625768/9c601fda4f673aaddf2c50434155a27d3a2d9d8c.jpg[/img]

By learning additional crew skills, you’ll unlock new types of [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1386780/view/3001068340439566546]backroom operations[/url] specifically designed to support the growth and upkeep of your vehicle fleet like garages and truck repair bays. These can be useful additions to your business empire particularly if you are going after the [i]producer of alcohols[/i] and [i]distributor to the people[/i] end game goals within the [b]economy category[/b].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38625768/c5d01c5e5ee97b63533a12155b12bfe4499e96ff.png[/img]

Once a delivery is up and running you can freely edit and reorder the steps and change crew members and vehicles.  

[u][b]Update: New industrial buildings[/b][/u]

You may have seen in our last update that skyscrapers have been added to the commercial and residential areas of each city map. To complement this we’ve just put in a load of large factory models which will spawn in and around industrial areas. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38625768/48c0ca8a9f29b4d425947b3bd8c6b088d0f75632.jpg[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38625768/8a215386f99c7b910af3327a8a90191d2eb91a40.jpg[/img]

We’re excited to see the elaborate production chains and networks that you’ll be creating  with these tools! So make sure to follow us on [url=https://twitter.com/CityOfGangsters]Twitter[/url] and join our [url=https://discord.com/invite/CityofGangsters]Discord[/url] to share your screenshots with the rest of the community. 

Until next time!

Matt & Rob
Co-founders - SomaSim

notes.title: City of Gangsters Developer Update #6
notes.content:
Hi everyone, just five weeks left until the launch of [i][b]City of Gangsters[/b][/i]! As we’re working on the final stages of development, we really wanted to keep these updates coming, and today we’re going to talk a bit about managing the many businesses you’ll acquire over the course of the game.

[u][b]Managing Businesses[/b][/u]

[b]Businesses[/b] are at the heart of your economy as they support the production, distribution and sale of valuable [b]alcohol resources[/b]. Each business has a legal side (a cover), and room in the back to install an [b]operation[/b] of your choice. 

The legal side of a business will often yield valuable resources over time, for example a [i]fruit stand[/i] might produce 8 barrels of [i]grape juice[/i] every 7 turns, which you can repurpose for some other use.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38625768/7b81e6cfcf0d72aead6231967f776f803300e077.png[/img]

In this way, legal businesses can be useful assets for supporting some of your more complex production chains as they generate resources without requiring input.

Most backroom operations on the other hand require a steady supply of ingredients and resources to maintain their production and sales. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38625768/fe32c0e2355ff14f7ce37eaf7fa36b487020cc02.png[/img]

You can see that this [i]sparkling cider operation[/i] requires [i]sugar[/i], [i]hard cider[/i], and [i]small bottles[/i] in order to refine 80 bottles of [i]sparkling cider[/i] every 12 turns.

[u][b]Acquiring businesses and setting up operations  [/b][/u]

By gaining territory and [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1386780/view/3099017193082394705]maintaining positive relationships with your contact network[/url] you’ll gain favors, and you can leverage those to learn about and acquire new businesses. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38625768/3a9a0233629870c96dd6404744e515005d48e94f.png[/img]

To install a backroom operation within an owned business you’ll first need money, materials, and the appropriate crew skills.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38625768/c9da557df6b8de3a0cfd1dffa3458c8ed83862d5.png[/img]

Here a [i]backroom winery[/i] requires $3500, 10 crates of [i]pipes[/i], 40 [i]barrels[/i], and 15 crates of [i]bricks[/i]. Your outfit must also have learned the [i]grape presses[/i] and [i]backroom winemaking[/i] crew skills.   

[u][b]Types of backroom operations[/b][/u]

In the course of the game you’ll discover loads of different operations to unlock, and they broadly fall into 3 categories:
  
[list]
[*] [b]Production operations[/b] - Presses, distilleries, stills, bottling and manufacturing operations which refine ingredients into valuable alcohol resources.    
[*] [b]Logistics operations[/b] - Garages, depots, and repair bays that support the expansion and upkeep of your vehicle fleet.  
[*] [b]Sales operations[/b] - Bootleggers, speakeasies, and clubs which sell alcohol resources for a tidy profit. 
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38625768/1ee9b0c97ecfd148a4977a2ae6ecc8a0bbc0887c.png[/img]

[u][b]Managers, expansions, and upgrades [/b][/u]

Each backroom operation can be improved by employing one of your crew members as its manager. Managers allow you to add expansions which improve production efficiency and resource yield. Some expansions require managers to have [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1386780/view/3024711605410615488]specific traits[/url], such as intelligent or hardworking ([i]production tracking[/i]), and talkative, friendly, or kind ([i]more bar seating[/i]).  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38625768/a1de18d9b710c273833d5b59303e20ecd0729f32.png[/img]

Upgrades allow you to improve your operations: increase alcohol production efficiency, increase the fleet capacity of logistics operations, or expand the drinks menu for sales operations, and so on. Some upgrades will require managers to have some experience in certain specializations, such as [i]manufacturing juice[/i] when upgrading a [i]juice press[/i].   

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38625768/e88f0cf16a7b2d19180414f11d781b1fe02663df.png[/img]

[u][b]Update: New skyscraper models[/b][/u]

[url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/423580/Project_Highrise/]Maybe we’re a little biased[/url] but it’s great to finally see skyscrapers appearing in-game. They are present in each of the base game’s three cities (Chicago, Pittsburgh, and Detroit), they tend to cluster around the more urban downtown areas of each map, and they present unique opportunities that don’t happen in lower-density areas of the city - so drive around and explore!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38625768/a00879048e6ac870d2ca8f24a1bb8c53228f388c.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38625768/151884dcc4e261291543935cf718eeb95b0e2ff3.png[/img]

That’s all for now but we’ll be back with another update very soon, and as always you can find us here, and on [url=https://discord.com/invite/CityofGangsters]Discord[/url] or [url=https://twitter.com/CityOfGangsters]Twitter[/url] if you have any questions.

notes.title: City of Gangsters Developer Update #2
notes.content:
Hi everyone, we’re back with another developer update. Today we’re going to focus on the [b]relationships[/b] that you will be building with the [b]businesses [/b]within your growing network of contacts. We’ll also be sharing progress on the game’s second city map, [b]Pittsburgh[/b]!

[u][b]Business relationships[/b][/u]

Social currency is a big deal in [i][b]City of Gangsters[/b][/i] and effectively managing the relationships with individual businesses will be a key part of spreading your influence across the city.    

Your relationship with each NPC business is the sum total of the interactions you had with that person - your various positive or negative actions towards them, the history of your business deals together, but also the gossip they overheard about what you’ve done to other people. On top of that, personal traits and your crew’s experience will modulate the relationship further. You can see how that is displayed in the UI, in the screenshot below.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38625768/4ef0e01436a6c496d75ed7ebecc100044ca0aebc.png[/img]

So what are the advantages of a positive relationship and the disadvantages of a negative one?

This is the time of Prohibition, and booze is illegal, so in order to get anything done, you have to be trusted by the people you’re dealing with. You have to build and maintain a positive relationship.

But when you meet a new business for the first time, your relationship will start around 0 (neutral). At this stage you have very few options - they don’t trust you enough to participate in any illegal deals just yet. However, if you can get them to warm up to you, whether through mutual friends or by showing that you’re on the level, you’ll start to see a much more diverse array of options.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38625768/6893028c1cafab767e09e8aa1d71f79e20b909d2.png[/img]

[u][b]Benefits of a positive relationship[/b][/u]

[b]Gain favors -[/b] Favors are an invaluable resource that can be spent in a wide variety of ways to open up new social and business opportunities for your outfit, e.g. learning about a special event or getting a trusted introduction to someone new.

[b]Open up illegal trade -[/b] Unlock access to a wider pool of tradable resources with the business. This is how you’ll be able to start selling the alcohol that you produce.

[b]Set up a front -[/b] Fronts are the catalysts for territory expansion and will collect protection money from local businesses. NPCs who run fronts for your outfit will often be your strongest allies. 

[b]Set up exclusive trade deals -[/b] Prevent rival outfits from trading with the business for a set number of turns. Just don’t be surprised when rivals will try to do the same to you.

[b]Learn new crew skills -[/b] Improve your outfit’s knowledge which will unlock entirely new production chains and opportunities.

[b]Learn about new properties -[/b] Expand your operational capacity by purchasing new businesses and starting new production locations, bootlegging operations, speakeasies, and so on.

[u][b]Disadvantages of a negative relationship [/b][/u]

[b]Refusal to do business -[/b] If the business owner dislikes and distrusts you, they will refuse to deal with you. So if you have only one supplier of a key resource, it’s crucial to keep them on your side.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38625768/0e87f7aaf5392b1490c991ef8e866e1945af90d1.png[/img]

[b]Reputation damage among friends and family - [/b]People will talk to their friends and family about their interactions with you. Whether your actions were altruistic or ruthless, you can be sure that the news will spread. So you’ll need to be careful who you upset, because they might have bigger friends who could give you real problems! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38625768/51594070cd2163ee431bcb2d137c1b55f1e95607.png[/img]

So which actions impact the relationship level?

[u][b]Positive actions[/b][/u]

[b]Doing legal and illegal business -[/b] Buying and selling with an NPC will create a small positive impression. But trading in illegal goods will boost the relationship much higher.

[b]Offer good deals on tradeable resources -[/b] Offering % discounts is a show of good faith which will be appreciated. 

[b]Completing missions -[/b] Depending on the context of your existing relationship, some NPC businesses will ask if you could help them out in various ways, and they will warm up to you considerably and show their gratitude if you succeed.

[b]Getting a trusted recommendation -[/b] Favors accumulated with other people can be redeemed to gain trusted introductions to new contacts, or improve relationships with existing mutual friends.

[b]Defending your people -[/b] Whether it’s helping a local business that’s being harassed by hooligans, or helping out the poor and needy in the community, small acts of benevolence can have a very positive impact.

[b]Helping a mutual friend -[/b] Remember, people talk, and the news of your good deeds is sure to spread.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38625768/ac8ca953d448b65ad7717e84f79bee932e49d2df.png[/img]

[u][b]Negative actions [/b][/u]

[b]Demanding higher prices on tradeable resources -[/b] Adding % premiums on resources that you trade will annoy the business. 

[b]Extortion -[/b] Demanding protection money from businesses within your territory will damage your relationship with them over time.  

[b]Destroying property -[/b] Some businesses will resist extortion but can be coerced into complying by trashing their place in various creative ways. This aggressive action will make them fear and loathe you in equal measure.

[b]Physical harm -[/b] This goes without saying, but people will remember any physical violence you do against them. The more serious the harm, the worse the effect.

[b]Hurting somebody’s friends and family -[/b] If you hurt someone’s brother or extort their cousin, that news will spread and affect your reputation. So be careful when you throw your weight around.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38625768/540fadc56684e5bca75b5adbbf3a0779ef8bb0a3.png[/img]

In future posts we’ll look at character traits and how relationships work with the police, local troublemakers and rival gangs, but for now, we hope that this has given you an insight into the fundamental social aspects of the game’s design.

[u][b]Update: Pittsburgh map visuals and unique resources [/b][/u]

With [i][b]City of Gangsters[/b][/i] we wanted to make a game that would have a high degree of replayability and from day one we planned to include [b]three city maps[/b] that would each present a different experience. If you’ve been keeping up with coverage of the game so far you will be familiar with the [b]Chicago[/b] map, which represents the core game. We’ve now turned our attention to the second of these maps, [b]Pittsburgh[/b], adding unique 3D models with architecture specific to that city, such as the colorful houses below.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38625768/1070b129483d17f75f0cbc6e8f37b0e57640dd3d.png[/img]

The map also contains new resources linked to the production of two alcohol recipes that are unique to the city, [b]Applejack[/b] and [b]Rakija[/b].   

[b]Applejack (Apple juice + small bottles + ice) -[/b] [i]Jacking is an old technique that uses cold temperatures induced by ice or snow or other cold temperatures to extract alcohol. It takes longer than distillation, but is considerably easier and cheaper. And not at all prone to explode.[/i]

[b]Rakija (Plums + small bottles + sugar) -[/b] [i]Immigrants from certain parts of Europe are sure to appreciate and pay handsomely for a potent taste of home, made from distilled plum juice. [/i]

Thanks again for stopping by and as always, come say hi on [url=https://discord.com/invite/CityofGangsters]Discord[/url] and follow us on [url=https://twitter.com/CityOfGangsters]Twitter[/url] for all the latest news and updates.

Matt & Rob
Co-founders - SomaSim

notes.title: City of Gangsters Developer Update #1
notes.content:
Hey everybody and welcome to the first of our developer updates! From now until launch we will be sharing more frequent updates with you on the progress of [i][b]City of Gangsters[/b][/i]. In these posts we’ll be getting into some of the game’s core mechanics as well as sharing recently added content which we hope you’ll enjoy. 

[u][b]The foundations of an empire.[/b][/u]

Today we’re going to talk a little bit about the foundations of your empire, and the kinds of basic alcohol that you’re going to be producing in the early parts of the game. [b]Homemade Booze[/b] is the lowest hanging fruit and is cheap and easy to manufacture. These are beverages that would have been commonly seen during Prohibition. In [i][b]City of Gangsters[/b][/i] each of our city maps will have its own unique variants of alcohol resources. For now let’s focus on Chicago where [b]Homemade Booze[/b] comes in four flavors: Homemade beer, Hard Cider, Brick Wine, and Moonshine. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38625768/a13691f99adb43815a0b6e781d1a81bd37df0273.png[/img]

Each of these can be produced at a business you control by installing the relevant back-room operation. You’ll notice that all four types of alcohol consist of a base ingredient (neutral alcohol, malt syrup, grape concentrate, apple juice) and a container (stoneware crocks).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38625768/48eeb024ca3d4326274b82de6a5df310491d4b12.png[/img]

Now while crocks are abundant throughout the city, other ingredients can be a little harder to come by. Over time you’ll acquire the skills and knowhow to build your own presses, processers, and distilleries to refine these ingredients. But should you ever find yourself with a short-term supply issue you can bet that someone you know will be happy to help out (with a few greenbacks on the side to sweeten the deal of course!).   

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38625768/87b99e2c753c0cacd0fbd54f1d8a36e4d99234f8.png[/img]

Aside from the different ingredients required to make them, the market value of each type of[b] Homemade Booze[/b] varies as well: 

Homemade beer - $8 per crock
Hard cider - $12 per crock
Brick wine - $15 per crock
Moonshine - $20 per crock

You’ll see that Moonshine is considerably more lucrative than homemade beer, but like many aspects of [i][b]City of Gangsters[/b][/i], the locations and level of demand from businesses for a particular resource is entirely procedurally generated, so each new game will present its own challenges and opportunities.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38625768/d1b207c407ccc6c86f1ff96e2f74608f93bc6ac8.png[/img]

Depending on the situation then, it might not necessarily be the best strategy to pursue the production of a higher value resource immediately. Instead, your best bet will be to look at the situation, work your connections, and adapt as events unfold…. 

[u][b]Updates: City Districts and new 3D models. [/b][/u]

We’ve recently added city districts to our city maps. Certain buildings and landmarks will be attached to certain districts to give you a better sense of the geography of the city that you are playing in.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38625768/a647da19a302fe6f2c55963f60a603d5632678de.png[/img]

Our 3D artist has also been hard at work on additional models to inject more character into the game world. We’re personally huge fans of the civic buildings (there are a few of this style still standing in Chicago if you know where to look!). Certain buildings will grant outfits that capture them special privileges, the details of which we will share with you later down the line… 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38625768/10b5aa8244810801f86fc27117095ddadea33ecc.png[/img]

That’s all for now, but we’ll be back with another update in a few weeks. In the meantime come hang out with us on [url=https://discord.com/invite/CityofGangsters]Discord[/url] and [url=https://twitter.com/CityOfGangsters]Twitter[/url]. 

Matt & Rob
Co-founders - SomaSim
